item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q009_heme_bundle_fold_not_homology","answer":"No. SCOPe places transmembrane di-heme cytochromes, fumarate-reductase respiratory-complex transmembrane subunits, and respiratory nitrate-reductase gamma chains in separate superfamilies within the heme-binding four-helical-bundle fold, in the membrane and cell surface proteins and peptides class. Their shared fold describes structural architecture; it does not establish common ancestry across these three groups. Separate superfamilies indicate that SCOPe does not assert that relationship, rather than proving that distant homology is impossible.\n\nA superfamily groups proteins with evidence supporting common ancestry; a family represents a more closely related grouping within it. Neither the shared fold nor the broader class justifies combining these proteins into one homologous family or superfamily. Heme binding and membrane electron transfer also do not justify transferring fumarate-reductase or nitrate-reductase complex membership, substrate specificity, or physiological electron partners between them. A cross-superfamily structural template may inform overall architecture, but detailed heme ligation, packing, and functional assignments require independent validation. One representative cannot establish homology or functional equivalence for all three groups.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
